alt: Kingdom of Lower Burgundy and Provence

predecessors.name: Middle Francia
predecessors.text: Charles of Provence's kingdom: 'Lower Burgundy with Provence' (Cliopatria's 860 shape minus the Lotharingian part it keeps from 866, but with the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble, which…

successors.name: Upper Burgundy
successors.text: Provence and the Rhône-Saône lands; Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy receives them from Hugh of Italy in 933 and unites the two Burgundies

rulers.name: Hugh of Arles (Hugh of Italy)
rulers.title: king of Italy, ruling Provence de facto

ledger.x: 855: Charles, youngest son of Lothair I, receives Lower Burgundy with Provence.
863: the bishoprics of Lyon, Vienne and Grenoble pass to Lothair.
863: Arles, Aix and Embrun pass to Louis II.
879: Boso is elected king of Lower Burgundy and Provence.
880: Louis III and Carloman II take Mâcon and the north of Boso's realm.
882: Boso is 'restricted to the county of Vienne'; by 882 he had already lost much of his Burgundian domains.
887: Charles the Fat confirms the young Louis in Provence.
905: Louis breaks his oath and invades Italy again.
905: 21 July, Louis is captured at Verona and blinded; he 'was forced to give up his Italian and imperial crowns'.
928: Louis the Blind dies (5 June) and Hugh of Arles takes the crown.
931: Hugh buys off Rudolph II with Viennois and Lyonnais.
933: Hugh gives Provence to Rudolph II.

wars.name: Charles the Bald's intervention in Provence
wars.outcome: Charles the Bald 'attempted to intervene in Provence in 861' but 'only reached Macon, being restrained by Hincmar of Rheims'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Carolingian war against Boso
wars.outcome: Louis III and Carloman II take Mâcon and the north after the Amiens division of March 880 (undated); the siege of Vienne (August-November 880, with Charles the Fat) fails; Richard the Justiciar takes Vienne in September 882 and confines Boso to the county of…

wars.name: Louis the Blind's Italian campaigns
wars.outcome: Louis is crowned King of Italy at Pavia (12 October 900) and emperor (901), is driven out by Berengar in 902, and is captured and blinded at Verona on 21 July 905.

wars.name: Hugh of Italy against Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy
wars.outcome: Hugh 'unsuccessfully attempted to take Burgundy from Rudolph's son, Rudolph II', buys him off with the Viennois and Lyonnais in 931 and cedes Provence in the treaty of 933.

certainty.note: The realm is described by ecclesiastical provinces (Arles, Aix, Vienne, Lyon), not by surveyed lines; the Italian frontier of 900-905 and the Burgundian frontier of 931-933 are approximate.
